# hoop_sidecar (Data Source)

Reads a sidecar by name. A sidecar that a `hoop_sidecar_service_account` identity created on its first handshake has no `hoop_sidecar` resource; this data source gives rule resources its id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

# A sidecar the gke-eu service account identity created on its first
# handshake, named by that account's name_template.
data "hoop_sidecar" "gke_eu_ws_123" {
  name = "gke-eu-ws-123"
}

resource "hoop_guardrail" "no_destructive" {
  name = "no-destructive"

  sidecar_spec = jsonencode({
    rules = [{ name = "no-destructive", type = "operation", operations = ["delete", "drop"] }]
  })

  sidecar_targets = [{ sidecar_id = data.hoop_sidecar.gke_eu_ws_123.id, listener_name = "appdb" }]
}

output "gke_eu_ws_123_config_state" {
  value = data.hoop_sidecar.gke_eu_ws_123.config_state
}

# The pods behind the sidecar, each with its status. Null until one reports.
output "gke_eu_ws_123_pods" {
  value = data.hoop_sidecar.gke_eu_ws_123.instances == null ? [] : [
    for i in data.hoop_sidecar.gke_eu_ws_123.instances : "${i.name} ${i.status}"
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The sidecar name.

### Read-Only

- `bound_rules` (Attributes List) The rules the control plane folds into this sidecar's configuration, and the listener each lands on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bound_rules))
- `config_state` (String) What the sidecar runs relative to the stored configuration. See `hoop_sidecar`.
- `configuration` (String) The stored configuration document, as JSON, without `load_from_disk`.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the sidecar, for `sidecar_targets`.
- `identity_issuer` (String) The issuer of the service account identity bound to this sidecar, if one reached it.
- `identity_subject` (String) The subject of the service account identity bound to this sidecar, if one reached it.
- `instances` (Attributes List) The pods behind this sidecar, one per hostname that reported to the control plane, ordered by name. They share one configuration and one identity; this lists which of them are up and what each runs. Null when none has reported, or on a gateway from before instances. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances))
- `last_error` (String) Why the sidecar refused the last configuration, or why the control plane did not serve it.
- `last_seen_at` (String) When the sidecar last handshook, RFC 3339. Empty until it does.
- `load_from_disk` (Boolean) Whether the sidecar runs its own config file.
- `version` (String) The sidecar binary version reported at the last handshake.

<a id="nestedatt--bound_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bound_rules`

Read-Only:

- `kind` (String) `guardrail`, `datamasking` or `analyzer`.
- `listener_name` (String) The listener the rule is bound to.
- `name` (String) The rule name.


<a id="nestedatt--instances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances`

Read-Only:

- `applied_revision` (String) The revision of the configuration the pod last applied.
- `last_error` (String) Why the pod refused the last configuration. Empty when it applied.
- `last_outcome` (String) What the pod did with the last configuration it received, such as `applied`.
- `last_seen_at` (String) When the pod last reached the control plane, RFC 3339.
- `name` (String) The hostname the pod reports.
- `status` (String) `online` when the pod reported recently, else `offline`.
- `version` (String) The sidecar binary version the pod runs.
